title: This feast of pure reason
html_source: At the end of the nightmare that is Circe, one picture of depravity after another, Bloom offers Stephen his ashplant (walking stick). Stephen responds, “Stick, no. Reason. This feast of pure reason.” What can his meaning be but an abject dismissal and refutation of a society whose intellectual elite has championed a devotion to “pure reason,” only to see in the end, not only an utter paucity of morals, but of any sign of reason, as well.
